source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: K · Long Island had the highest average price at $42.54/MWh, followed by J · New York City ($39.77/MWh) and H · Millwood ($37.84/MWh).
K · Long Island's average price was $10.70/MWh above the cheapest zone, A · West ($31.84/MWh).
K · Long Island had the heaviest congestion: on average it added $6.32/MWh to the price, ahead of J · New York City ($3.74/MWh) and H · Millwood ($2.09/MWh).

Congestion lowered the average price in A · West (by $0.57/MWh), B · Genesee (by $0.24/MWh) and D · North (by $0.87/MWh), consistent with power being trapped on the generating side of transmission limits.
All 3 highest-price zones are also among the 3 most congested: K · Long Island, J · New York City and H · Millwood.
Across all zone-months, heavier congestion tends to come with higher prices: a strong correlation (r = -0.65).
The link is strongest in Capital & Hudson Valley (F–I) (r = -0.83) and weakest in Upstate (A–E) (r = -0.15).
The most extreme single 5-minute congestion value was -$4,000.00/MWh in K · Long Island (Apr 2024), far beyond its monthly average.
cannot_conclude: Higher congestion in a zone does not tell us which transmission line was the bottleneck.
Congestion and price moving together does not prove congestion caused the higher price; weather, fuel prices and demand affect both.
Average $/MWh cannot be turned into total dollars paid, because zone electricity usage is not in this data.
